title: Is there a market for a Unity developer focused on small projects using AI-assisted development?
author: ThaiSpanish
selftext:
I'm trying to figure out whether there is a realistic market for the kind of work I can offer.

I've recently finished my first small mobile game/app in Unity completely by myself, from concept to Google Play.

The project is fairly simple technically: it's a 2D/mobile game based around UI, images, multiple-choice questions/puzzles, progression, audio, ads, save system, QA, Android build and Play Store publishing.

I used AI tools extensively as a development assistant, both for coding and for creating some of the visual content. The important part is that I handled the integration, testing, debugging and overall product myself.

I'm now wondering whether there is actually a market for this kind of service:

**small Unity projects developed quickly with AI-assisted workflows**, particularly for indie developers, small businesses, prototypes, educational apps, interactive experiences, simple mobile games, etc.

I'm not looking to build large or technically complex games. I'm more interested in taking relatively simple ideas and turning them into functional, polished Unity applications quickly.

For those of you who freelance or hire Unity developers:

**Is this a type of service people actually pay for?**  
  
**What kind of clients would you target for this?**

**Would you market yourself as a Unity developer and simply mention AI-assisted development as part of your workflow, or would you explicitly offer it as a service?**

And finally, where would you look for these kinds of small projects?

Pd: I let a small video of my project, after learning to do this, I will create some puzzle game based on pixelart. Can't hear in the audio but also has sound effects and music.

comments.author: heavy-minium
comments.body: Not really, there are far too many people that will be able to do that themselves. It's not just your price - it's a lot of work to delegate too, so this needs to pay off - and in your case, the skills you bring on the table are not enough to warrant that cost.

replies.author: ThaiSpanish
replies.body: I was even asking for short-small projects. Anyways, I guess is time to change my career 🤣🥲

replies.author: ThaiSpanish
replies.body:
And what do you mean by “a lot of work to delegate too”? Like, that’s why I am using AI, the art, the code, workflow, debugging, etc.

All of that, can be done by just one person with the correct knowledge of how to ask to an AI. But maybe, there are clients out there that would like to develop smth but they don’t know the tools. So maybe, they’d pay to people like me to develop their basic ideas to convert them in functional stuff.

comments.author: Gigaslavx
comments.body: Not really, the market is oversaturated with supply. A lot of ex gamers are trying game dev now. Don't take me wrong it still takes expertise to cook up a simple game so the goal posts are moved a simple game is not enough now if you want financial success. You can still do it in your free time for fun instead of gaming, I mean playing games didn't bring money right if anything you spent, so now you're like paying to create

replies.author: ThaiSpanish
replies.body: XD well, I am not a gamer at all. Been working in the industry for 5 years, and have participated in gamejams. Now with AI I can do things I can’t before cuz I am not a programmer. But cool, I understand!
